results.title: Road Conditions - Ontario_511
results.description:
Ontario 511 is a bilingual digital traveller information service provided by the Ontario Ministry of Transportation. The goal is to present public information that impacts provincial highway travel in order to improve safety and reduce congestion. In 1986, the Ministry of Transportation offered their first traveller information service to the public with a winter road conditions telephone hotline. In 1999, the ministry expanded the service by launching a Road Condition Website. By 2004, the service evolved into the Traveller Road Information Portal (TRIP) website and offered an interactive telephone service.
 
In 2013 the service was launched as “Ontario 511”. It has been enhanced to provide 24/7 access to bilingual and accessible highway travel information through multiple channels – mobile app, website, X and telephone.
 
Sources
 
This service was created using the Ontario 511 API

Metadata:
Events
Construction
Cameras
Road Conditions

 
Workflow
Using a Notebook, road event information is parsed from the the Ontario 511 json, and used to populate the attribute tables of the  EventPoints, ConstructionProjects, Cameras, and RoadConditions layers.

 
Update Frequency: Every 15 minutes
 

 
Contact Information
 
  • For inquiries on the data, contact Ontario 511
  • For inquires regarding the service, please leave a comment below

results.title: Daily Foot Traffic Downtown San Rafael
results.description:
This downloadable dataset contains daily foot traffic at intersections on 4th Street in downtown San Rafael. Foot traffic count are obtained from Miovision Cameras. Daily Foot Traffic is the number of times an intersection was crossed each day. Foot traffic is not a count of individual pedestrians – Miovision cameras cannot differentiate between individuals.

Miovision traffic cameras used by the City of San Rafael capture only information that is pertinent to tracking the movement and classification of vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians over short period (12-72 hours). Cameras capture at a video resolution low enough to ensure faces, license plates, and other features are not recognizable. There is no recording of sound and cameras are angled to capture only approach lanes and pedestrian crossings.

Once videos are captured, they are uploaded to Miovision’s website where they are stored and processed using automated detection zones similar to video detection technology used for traffic signals. The City of San Rafael data team pulls data from Miovision once daily, aggregates the pedestrian counts from 15 minute intervals to daily intervals, and uploads the information to the open data portal. Data from Miovision does not contain identifying information.

The latitude and longitude of each intersection can viewed here.

results.title: 2015 Traffic Count Data
results.description:
2015 Traffic Count Program Report

 General

In 2015, the BHJ Transportation Study, as part of its regional transportation planning role, obtained traffic count data at various locations throughout the study area.  These traffic counts may be the result of specific study requests or data needed to assist in the overall planning process.  Beginning in 2006, the agency organized its traffic counting program to count specific locations in the region every three years.  Specific locations obtained in 2015 are for program cycle year one which are generally a repeat of locations obtained in 2006, 2009, and 2012. This completes the tenth year of this traffic counting program.

 In West Virginia, traffic counts were obtained on various routes in Hancock County and relevant routes heading into and out of Brooke and Hancock counties. In Ohio, traffic counts were obtained on various routes heading into and out of Jefferson County and at locations in Steubenville. Some of the count locations in Jefferson County are also travel demand model screen line routes.  Also, counts were obtained at locations in Ohio which were requested by the Ohio Department of Transportation (ODOT) for their Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) reporting required by the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA).

 Most of the traffic counts were obtained in 15 minute interval resolution and generally for a minimum of 24 hours.  Counts obtained with hose type counters generally ran for just over 48 hours. Counts obtained with plate type counters generally ran for 24 hours.

 During the 2015 calendar year, a total 497 counts were obtained.  Twenty-nine counts were attempted but failed due to counter malfunctions, installation failure or detector failure (traffic signal system counts). The majority of the non-signal system locations were re-counted during the year.

Traffic Signal System Data

The City of Steubenville and the Village of Wintersville have traffic signal systems that use count data gathered from video and inductive loop detectors to adjust the timing and relationships of adjacent traffic signals for smoother traffic flow. The agency contacted both jurisdictions and obtained permission to gather some of this traffic count data on a regular basis. Currently, data have been obtained from the City of Steubenville. Data obtained from Wintersville was incomplete and BHJ is working to resolve this issue with Village officials.

The count data from Steubenville was extracted for a representative week from each quarter of the year (January, April, July and October). Daily totals from each of the count stations are included in the overall report summaries shown in Table One, Two and Three. Examples of detailed reports developed by BHJ are shown in Appendix B. These reports are on file for each count station and may be obtained upon request.

Counting Equipment

At the end of 2015, the following inventory of counting units were operational.

·         Four (4) Nu-Metric NC-97 plate type counters

·         Four (4) Vaisala NC-200 plate type counters

·         Seven (7) Diamond Apollo 4 channel hose type counters

·         Sixteen (16) Diamond Omega 2 channel hose type counters

·         One (1) Jamar acoustic counter

 Plate type counters work well where data from a specific lane is desired.  Plate counter units have been used at large intersections to count right turning traffic by placing the unit out of the through travel lanes in the corner radius area.  The units are also useful on four lane streets and high speed roadways.  They are more easily deployed and retrieved than hose counters.  Because they are also smaller in size, they are more easily transported.  The downside of plate counters is their susceptibility to theft and damage if they come loose from the pavement.  The accuracy of plate counters is somewhat variable so they are only deployed in situations described above.

 Hose type counters are the work horse of BHJ’s counting equipment fleet and are proven technology.  In fact the technology has advanced to the point where little or no trouble is ever experienced with the hose transducers (the device in the unit that senses the vehicle via the hose).  Years ago, the hose interface was the “Achilles’ heel” of this equipment.  Hose counters have the capability to accurately classify vehicles and measure vehicle speeds.  Because the units can be chained and locked to poles, trees or guardrail posts, they are more resistant to vandalism than plate units.  The downside is the units require the placement of hoses across the pavement being counted which creates a challenge to keep them in place especially on high speed roadways.  Also, the hoses take up considerable space in the transport vehicle.  In an attempt to address this, in 2012 the agency decided to migrate to “low profile” hose which takes less space for storage. The downside is these hoses are less robust and therefore wear out more quickly.  However, had the agency stayed with the traditional larger hose, it would have been impossible to haul all the hose needed in the agency vehicle.

 The Jamar unit uses acoustic technology to detect vehicle engine and road noise, which it translates into a vehicle count.  It is mounted by strapping it to a tree or power pole aimed at the roadway about five feet above the surface.  There is no need to place anything on roadway.  The agency has found the unit to be accurate when used in environments where there is little chance of extraneous noise.  Therefore, this counter is mainly used for very low volume roads with gravel surfaces. Another downside is the data obtained is not directional. No traffic count studies were performed in 2015 using the Jamar unit.

 2015 Count Locations

 The count locations for 2015 are shown on the maps included in this document (Figures One through Three).  The number shown at each location identifies the MAP ID which is a cross reference shown in Summary Tables One through Three.  Data contained in the Summary Tables include the location, direction of traffic counted, date of the survey, 24 hour traffic volume total (unadjusted), jurisdiction, county, state and the traffic count filename.  Table One (1) is indexed by MAP ID, Table Two (2) is indexed by Count Location Reference and Table Three (3) is indexed by the Count Filename.

 Mechanical traffic count information sheets are shown in Appendix B.  These sheets are used during the traffic counting season to organize counting activities and keep track of count locations and the counting equipment used for each study site.

 Data from each traffic count are maintained in ESRI® ArcMap™ GIS mapping software. The data fields for each count record are shown in Appendix C.

 The agency continues to use the field hardened tablet computer obtained in 2013 for use in documenting count locations. The tablet uses the Microsoft© Windows 7 operating system and has a built-in GPS for location positioning and a camera for field documentation.  The tablet unit replaces a dedicated GPS unit used by the agency for several years.  The advantage of the tablet is a larger screen making field input much easier and data is easily sync’ed with office files over the office network using a standard WiFi connection.

results.name: Right_of_Way_Lane_Closures_For_The_City_of_Austin_WFL1
results.title: Right of Way Lane Closures For The City of Austin - Working Directory
results.description:
Working Directory

This map of Austin includes overlaps of the street system and Traffic Analysis Zones. Dots representing locations where 24-hour traffic counts are available are also included. The user can click on a dot to see the potential closure hours for the selected count location. 

Potential closure times are specified as hours of the day using a 24-hour clock. Additional information about the count and location is provided in the table that appears after clicking a dot. 

The data for 24-Hour Volume Counts was obtain by comprising four primary sources: Traffic Studies: Vehicle Volume Reports (i.e. road tubes, City of Austin), Radar Traffic Counts (i.e. Wavetronix Radar Sensors, City of Austin), TXDOT Traffic Count Database System (TCDS), and Traffic Detectors (i.e. GRIDSMART Camera Traffic Counts, City of Austin). The Street Network is primarily made up of Street Centerline information from the City of Austin. The Traffic Analysis Zones (TAZs) are clipped to fit the City of Austin region.

These 24-hour counts reflect the traffic flow estimates from 2015 through 2019, but a three percent compounded annual growth rate has been used to convert all to equivalent 2019 values. Due to COVID-19 impacts since 2019, there has been no attempt to convert volumes to more recent years.

results.name: Weigh_Stations_Feature_Layer
results.title: Weigh Stations Feature Layer
results.description:
Weigh Stations:

Weigh stations layer created for the ITS & Signals Management Group as part of the ASI Non-STIP effort. Weigh Stations are roadside stations where commercial vehicles are required to stop or be inspected for excess weight or safety violations to keep roads safe. This data contains point locations of weigh stations and attributes of the stations such as route, division, type of station, station characteristics such as automated license plate readers, weigh in motion systems, CCTV cameras and more.

Field Descriptions:

 

  • WeighStation- Weigh Station location with directional description
  • Route- Interstate or road weigh station is located
  • Division- Division weigh station is within
  • Type- Virtual or physical weigh station (Virtual/Physical)
  • WIM- Weigh in Motion System (Yes/No)
  • ALPR- Automated License Plate Reader (Yes/No)
  • TACS- Tire Anomaly and Classification System (Yes/No)
  • DOTRead- USDOT Registration Number Reader (Yes/No)
  • CCTVCameras- Dedicated Weigh Stations CCTV cameras for monitoring the station ramps and/or upstream traffic (Yes/No)
  • Fiber Between Stations- Fiber-optic connection between the two scale houses of paired stations (Yes/No)
  • Fiber for Video- Fiber-optic connection to the NCDOT ITS network for the purpose of sharing video feeds from CCTV cameras (Yes/No/Connected)
  • SProject- Link to the current As-Built plans in SharePoint
  • GoogleLink- Link to the ariel view of the weigh station on Google Maps
  • WSName- Weigh station location name

Data Source and Creation: 

All data for the Weigh Stations Layer was obtained through field collection of a private firm under the supervision of the ITS & Signals Management Group. Any questions regarding data collection and validation process should be addressed towards them. 

This data is intended for use in the ATLAS (Advancing Transportation through Linkages, Automation, and Screening) Tool for the ITS & Signals Management Group at NCDOT.

results.title: Automated Speed Enforcement Camera Removal – Monitoring Speed Data
results.description:
Following the approval of Bill 56, Building a More Competitive Economy Act, 2025, all automated speed enforcement cameras were deactivated on November 13, 2025. The city has since been collecting and analyzing speed data at the original eight pilot locations to evaluate the impact of the camera removals. Monthly updates are provided for each site, including average speed, 85th percentile speed, speed-limit compliance rates, and the proportion of high-end speeders. This data is presented alongside baseline conditions prior to ASE camera installation and results observed during the enforcement period.

 

Date Created: January 2026
Update Frequency: Monthly
Accuracy, Completeness, and Known Issues: The Pre ASE Installation raw data for Site E007 Smyth was not found so the 85th percentile speed, compliance percentage and high end speeder percentage used for the Pre ASE Installation data type for site E007 are from The Automated Speed Enforcement Pilot-Technical Memo from August 27th 2021.
 

Attributes:    

  • Average Speed (AvgSpeed)
  • 85th percentile (Pct85th)
  • Compliance percentage (PctCompliance)
  • Percentage of high end speeders (PctHighEndSpeeders)

results.title: TrafficSignals
results.description:
Traffic Lights were collected as part of a pavement collection and analysis project wherein 360° camera images were captured and used as a visual, georeferenced record of the roadway and right-of-way to support visualization and asset inventory.

360 imagery was collected during the period of November-December, 2025.

Traffic Lights were one of the assets types collected using artificial intelligence (AI) review of the imagery.

AI-based mapping is not as exact as manually mapping by a technician; however, the resulting data is well suited for network-level inventory, planning, and asset awareness purposes. This approach provides a rapid, cost-effective means of identifying asset presence and approximate locations across the roadway network, enabling the City to establish a baseline inventory or supplement existing datasets. The data is most appropriate for high-level inventory, screening, and planning, with the understanding that precise positioning and attribute refinement would require additional manual QA/QC or field verification.

The attributes of interest include:

object_value – the identifying attribute value the AI software flagged as:

object--traffic-light--general-horizontal-back

object--traffic-light--general-horizontal-front

object--traffic-light--general-horizontal-side

object--traffic-light--general-single

object--traffic-light--general-single-front

object--traffic-light--general-upright

object--traffic-light--general-upright-back

object--traffic-light--general-upright-front

object--traffic-light--general-upright-side

object--traffic-light--other

object--traffic-light--pedestrians-back

object--traffic-light--pedestrians-front

first_seen_at – the date upon which the image containing the asset was taken.

results.name: hgdc_coverage
results.title: HERE GIS Data Suite coverage - layer
results.description:
Overview

HERE GIS Data Suite coverage layer provides a country-level overview of various HERE data product coverages.

Data Source

  • Original Data: The source data is exported as a CSV from the Tableau dashboard: Mosaic Content Summary / Country Content Summary v2.
  • CSV File: Mosaic Country Summary 2025Q2.csv

Coverage Calculation

  • For each country, the script checks for the presence and status of specific HERE data products (e.g., Advanced Map, HERE Places, 3D Buildings, etc.).
  • Coverage columns (e.g., Base Data Coverage, Places Coverage, etc.) are set to 1 (Yes) or 0 (No) based on the logic:
    • For most products, coverage is Yes if there is an entry for the product with Actual/Planned as Actual and Status as Yes or a positive value, depending on the product.

Attributes

  • Country (Text)
  • Region (Text)
  • Subregion (Text)
  • Release (Text)
  • Coverage columns (Short Integer):
    • Advanced Data Coverage
    • Base Data Coverage
    • Places Coverage
    • POIs Coverage
    • Building Footprint Coverage
    • Point Address Coverage
    • Micro Point Address Coverage
    • Traffic Pattern Coverage
    • Traffic Signals Stop and Signs Coverage
    • Speed Limit Coverage
    • Commercial Vehicle Regulations Coverage
    • Distance Markers Coverage
    • Safety Cameras Coverage
    • Cellular Signal Coverage
    • Unmaintained
  • Coverage Summary (Short Integer): 1 if any coverage column is 1, else 0 - used for symbology only

results.name: Pasco_Strategic_Plan_Counts
results.title: Pasco Strategic Plan Counts
results.description: Continuous count stations provide data users with information related to traffic volume, classification, speed, and more.  When developing a new count program, it is a best practice identify where existing/ incoming count stations are already located, to avoid duplicating data collection efforts.  The locations in this map layer display the 4 selected locations for traffic data collection.  The traffic data collected supports the 2025 Pasco County MPO Micromobility Strategic Plan and Data Collection Study.  These locations were selected based on a combination of roadway characteristics, land use characteristics, crash data, and other unique factors.  This study utilized smart camera traffic data collection technology, enhanced with artificial intelligence (AI) data processing to collect the traffic data.  A typical short-term smart camera data collection duration is 24 hours during a weekday (Thursday) and 24 hours during a weekend (Saturday).  The results of this data collection study will help determine if these sites are to remain as short-term count sites or eventual continuous count stations.

10/20/2020 Update Major

Fiber and electrical are being installed October 2020 at ASU Water Plant. While the ditches are open I collected images and exact location with a high accuracy GPS, EOS Arrow Gold the afternoon of 10/14/2020. The GPS worked very well in open sky, accuracy .2-.4 of an Inch; however, beside structures and under tree canopy the accuracy fell to around 6 feet After this data is imported into the GIS Portal attribution will follow from Facilities Electrical Department and Tec Support. While I was there I also collected obvious above ground structure. See below email string:

Scott EggersWed, Oct 14, 1:38 PM (21 hours ago)to me, Matt, Michael

Eddie,

ASU Electrical shop has been installing some infrastructure at the Water Plant on Rainbow Trail for some security cameras I believe. They are in the process of backfilling the trenches now.

We are putting 2-1" PVC from entrance gate all the way around the building to the exit gate for security cameras. There is a total of about 650' of ditch. It is open as of today but we will be backfilling tomorrow. If possible, it would be best to come out early in the morning tomorrow. Call me at (828)964-1698. Scott

10-4. Thanks Eddie

The Endzone, Raven Rocks, Laurel Hill, and Thunder Hill area has been updated 10/2/2020, from an As Built .dwg converted into feature classes. This conversion was done 7/12/2019. Field work was also done to fact check some of the features, as construction continues. As more information becomes available more edits will be done. Since Raven Rocks and Thunder Hill have been completed I thought they need to be represented. I should soon receive the finalized .dwg from the contactors. This is a living feature class that is edited and updated as information becomes available.

9/28/2020

Leon Levine Hall of Health Sciences, College of Health Sciences

These features were updated using a Bid Package 2, May 9, 2016, Page 21 C302, CERT. NO. 50417. This PDF was georeferenced, using ArcMap 10.8.1 on 9/24/2020 using known landmarks, and completed fieldwork from the fall of 2018. These updates may be changed again once the finalized DWG files are released. All associated documentation.

4/15/2019

Using new photography and the retaining wall feature class, as well as others, I have snapped surrounding features together as they should be. This procedure has taken sometime and I am sure I have missed some things but the vector basemap looks much cleaner now. I would have thought Rochester would have done this for us as a final draft of their services. All of the line features that should be a closed item are now. As I run across others they will be corrected as well.

3/23/2018 Updated

2/5/2018

12/12/17 I downloaded this Town of Boone Sidewalk layer from the town’s GIS Server. It appears this layer was created by Town of Boone GIS Department, (Chris Miller?) on 4/21/2015 no specific metadata is available. The polylines were broken at every intersection. For Appalachian State University proposes I felt we wanted whole polylines to represent sidewalks. For walking purposed it does not matter if is a sidewalk or a driveway. The main question is it safe for foot traffic. I proceeded to connect merge the polylines. Some data may have been lost combining the lines with respect to the condition of the sidewalks; however, this column appeared to be fairly sparse and the data is now over two years old. Today February the 2, 2018 I buffered the polylines to 2.5 feet since most of the Towns sidewalks are 5 feet with a .5 foot curb. The buffered lines now polygons have now been attributed and added to ASU sidewalk SDE.

10/9/2017 I edited the Greenwood Trail surface information and some added images. The path was mulch until sometime this summer when it was improved with a layer of added gravel that was roughly graded. The leaves covering the unevenly applied gravel in the path make for a less than even walking surface. This is a woods trail; I would not recommend persons that are not sure foot to use it.

3/6/2017 Editor Tracker has been added to this feature class. All of the attributes have been appropriately updated and meaningless columns omitted. However, this is a work in progress.

In this dataset 219 polygons were remotely sensed, throughout the Appalachian State University’s main campus, using aerial photography. The total shape length is 207,265 feet and the area is 981,469 square feet. It would be great if this attribute dataset included when the section of sidewalk was installed, and what the current condition of that section of sidewalk is. As of 07/28/2016 there is no information about when this data was acquired.

A new feature class Sidewalk_Hyle09192016 was created and completed, roughed out, on 09/21/2016. This allowed for all of the original data to stay in the Sidewalk feature class from Rochester. This new feature class better represents Appalachian State University sidewalks. All polygons have been named, classed, and condition roughly assessed. Many unnecessary polygons have been removed while many others have been created. This naming and classing of the attribute data came from memory, and viewing the 6-inch aerial photograph. There are currently 266 polygons with a total square footage of 883,702. Total square foot area of brick pavers is 252,220 square feet with 51 polygons selected, and concrete are 608,887 square feet with 208 polygons selected.

Woodard & Curran, Rochester & Associates, Inc. Edward Hyle
